content: Sanskrit is traditionally written in the Devanagari script. It consists of 13 vowels (Swaras) such as अ, आ, इ, ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, ए, ऐ, ओ, औ, and 33 primary consonants (Vyanjanas) organized phonetically by point of articulation (Guttural, Palatal, Retroflex, Dental, Labial).
Basic Sanskrit greetings are respectful and commonly used in daily conversation.

Sanskrit sentence structure typically follows Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order, although because inflections (vibhaktis) clearly define grammatical roles, word order in Sanskrit is relatively flexible.

examples.meaning: Rama (Subject) book (Object) reads (Verb) -> Rama reads the book.
